correctness.rationale: For \(F=-\sum_{j\ge0}x^{2^j}\), the identity \(F(x^2)-F(x)=x\) and factorization \(L=(\Phi-x)(\Phi-1)\) give \(L(F)=L(1)=0\). The classical Fredholm series is hypertranscendental. The splitting field is generated by \(F\), and every difference-Galois automorphism sends \(F\) to \(F+c\); hence the group embeds in the additive group and any parametrized refinement has differential dimension at most one. This correctly contradicts a universal dimension-two clause.
